caption: The drawing features three distinct depictions of a surveyor's compass (circumferentor) with different perspectives and arrangements. At the top center, a brass and glass circular compass is mounted on a wooden base with a vertical brass sight at each end, and it sits atop a section of a wooden tripod with brownish tones. The compass face is divided into segments, and markings and pointers are visible within the glass housing. To the lower left, there is a full view of the same instrument, showing the entire wooden tripod with three elongated legs spread out in a stable stance, and the compass unit positioned on top with the upright brass sights. At the lower right, a top-down view of the compass alone displays the face clearly, with its cardinal directions and segments marked, and brass attachments at the north and south positions. The composition is set against a beige background, and the illustration uses a realistic color palette with shades of brass, brown, green, and blue for metallic, wooden, and glass components.
title: Surveyor's Compass
